messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify quickSort correctly sorts a typical unsorted array (length > 1) in-place, exercising the full recursive path.
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the main recursive path is exercised, including partitioning and recursive calls, and verifies that the array is sorted and all elements are preserved. It detects bugs in partitioning, recursion, and in-place modification.

path_conditions: low < high (array has at least two elements, or subarray is nontrivial)

primary.name: quickSort
primary.signature: void quickSort(int arr[], int low, int high)

dependencies.name: partition
dependencies.signature: int partition(int arr[], int low, int high)
dependencies.reason: Required for partitioning step in quickSort

dependencies.name: quickSort
dependencies.signature: void quickSort(int arr[], int low, int high)
dependencies.reason: Recursive calls to itself for subarrays

assertions.name: assert_array_sorted
assertions.purpose: Verify the array is sorted in ascending order after quickSort
assertions.usage: After quickSort completes, check that the array is sorted

assertions.name: assert_array_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the sorted array contains the same elements as the original (permutation check)
assertions.usage: After sorting, compare sorted array to expected sorted array

utilities.name: create_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Allocate and initialize a test array with given values
utilities.usage: Setup: create the input array for sorting

utilities.name: helper_copy_int_array
utilities.purpose: Create a deep copy of an integer array for expected value/reference
utilities.usage: Setup: create a copy of the input array to sort and compare

utilities.name: cleanup_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Free memory allocated for the test array

preconditions: input_array is allocated and initialized with unsorted values
expected_sorted_array is a sorted copy of input_array
setup_requirements.initial_state: input_array contains unsorted integers; expected_sorted_array contains the same values in sorted order

primary_function_args.rationale: Triggers the main recursive path (low < high) and exercises partitioning and recursion
Sorts the entire array from the beginning
Sorts the entire array to the end

return_value.description: No return value; arr is sorted in-place

side_effects.effect: input_array is sorted in ascending order
input_array contains the same elements as before (permutation)

invariants_maintained: All original elements are present after sorting

assertions_required.description: Verify the array is sorted in ascending order after quickSort
Verify the sorted array contains the same elements as the original (permutation check)
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Elements lost, duplicated, or corrupted during sort

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All allocated arrays are freed; no memory leaks

operation_sequence: Create expected_sorted_array using helper_copy_int_array, then sort it (e.g., with qsort or manual sort)
Assert input_array is sorted using assert_array_sorted
Assert input_array equals expected_sorted_array using assert_array_equal
edge_cases_to_note: Array with duplicate values (e.g., two 5s) to check stability of element preservation
Array with minimum and maximum values
No NULL or empty array tested here (not this path)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Main recursive path: low < high, partition, recursive calls on subarrays

integration_test_suggestions: Test quickSort with already sorted array
Test quickSort with all elements equal
Test quickSort with array of size 1 and 0 (other paths)
